condition.label: rheumatoid arthritis
condition.distinctions: Inflammatory systemic RA differs from OA, nonspecific arthralgia or a single tendinopathy. Joint/site and damage are attributes.

scope.population: Adults with diagnosed RA; disease activity,joint damage/deformity and comorbidity alter applicability.
scope.stage: Stable treated low/moderate disease activity represented in recent HIIT RCT; severe flare, unstable disease or recent surgery not established.
scope.operativeStatus: Primarily nonoperative exercise research; surgical protocols and postoperative clearance not established.
scope.exclusions: RAPIT baseline-damage subgroup concern;2024 trial excludes cardiovascular/other limitations precluding HIIT. Trial eligibility is not a general prohibition.
scope.uncertainty: No diagnosis-only ban on resistance exercise, no universal pain cap or unrestricted loading established.

sources.population: RA adults; baseline large-joint damage subgroup highlighted; details not established from abstract.
sources.comparator: Two-year intensive RAPIT versus usual-care physical therapy.
sources.outcomes: MACTAR change difference year2 3.1 (95%CI0.7–5.5); HAQ −0.09 (−0.18 to−0.01). Overall median large-joint damage not increased; considerable baseline-damage group may progress more.
sources.uncertainty: Subgroup damage signal without accessible exact stratification; small HAQ difference.
sources.harms: No detrimental disease-activity effect reported; possible large-joint structural harm in considerable-baseline-damage subgroup.
sources.limitations: Cannot translate subgroup signal into all-RA weight cap; no fulltext protocol.

sources.population: RA>1year,stable antirheumatic medication3months,DAS28<5.1; prescreened rheumatologist/CPET, cardiovascular and participation-limiting comorbidity excluded.
sources.comparator: Advice moderate PA≥150min/week plus equipment-free home exercise; unequal supervision.
sources.coInterventions: Stable antirheumatic treatment; two participants later received corticosteroid injections and modified exercise.
sources.outcomes: VO2max difference3.71mL/kg/min (95%CI2.16–5.25). Pain −4.0 (−13.07 to5.06),DAS28 −0.25 (−0.60 to0.10): no significant differences. Fitness benefit is not proof of anti-inflammatory efficacy.
sources.uncertainty: Selected mostly female cohort,short follow-up,combined HIIT/strength,unequal contact; ClinicalTrials.gov registered retrospectively, Swedish registration prospectively.
sources.harms: One irregular-heart-rate episode required cardiology review and moderate-intensity continuation; four transient musculoskeletal pain cases modified exercise; one persistent-pain case stopped strength component.
sources.limitations: Not transferable to severe/unstable RA, all damaged joints, or unscreened HIIT.

protocol.execution: Cycle ergometer HIIT plus8individually adapted large-muscle strength exercises: examples leg press,squat,hip extension,pulldown,biceps curl,rows,sit-ups,lumbar extension; plus self-selected aerobic session.
protocol.frequency: Two supervised sessions and one40min70%HRmax aerobic session/week,12weeks.
protocol.supervision: Rheumatology-expert physiotherapists, groups8; rheumatologist/CPET screening and HR sensors.
protocol.stoppingRules: Trial allowed pain≤5/10;temporarily modified if>5 or>24h persistence;flare/joint effusion prompted rheumatology consultation. These are study-specific, not app defaults.

sources.design: EULAR evidence/consensus update; searches August2024,26-member task force, four principles and11recommendations.
sources.population: Inflammatory arthritis including RA/SpA and hip/knee OA; condition-specific adaptation still needed.
sources.coInterventions: Usual disease care; behavior change and physical-activity support.
sources.outcomes: Recommends assessment, individualized adaptation, competent delivery and explicit FITT-volume-progression; no single optimal execution.
sources.uncertainty: General PA applicability does not eliminate comorbidity/execution risk. Contraindication-for-PA-per-se wording cannot establish every exercise safe.
sources.harms: Discusses transient soreness versus joint symptoms and limited underlying harms data; not universal safety clearance.
sources.limitations: The24-hour rule is an example used in some studies;48–72hour soreness can occur. Neither is a validated universal stop threshold.

protocol.execution: Individualized aerobic,strength,flexibility and neuromotor activity; not an exact exercise.
protocol.dose: Specify individual frequency,intensity,time,type,volume and progression; no common patient dose.
protocol.supervision: Competent health professionals; delivery adapted to preferences.
protocol.progression: Lower tolerated starting dose in deconditioned/functionally limited participants and gradual increase.
protocol.stoppingRules: Consider symptomatic activity alternatives; no single validated numeric algorithm.

gaps: Independent clinical review absent. All mappings/rules/requests are candidates; no therapeutic release, clinical approval or universally safe exercise claim.
Source doses describe studied or recommended contexts, not individual app prescriptions. No generic five-second stretch progression or strength-set credit for stretching.
Coexisting conditions, equipment, independently selected joint limits and user-confirmed starting load remain separate constraints; no restriction may be relaxed to fill an empty workout.
RAPIT full methods,damage-stratum tables and separate hand/foot reports not extracted; no numeric large-joint damage/load threshold derived.
No validated self-directed flare/pain distinction or safe generic starting load; cardiovascular screening and individualized joint limits remain necessary research context.
